results.title: Reggae Boyz squad named for opening Nations League games
results.description: Head Coach Rudolph Speid has named his Reggae Boyz squad for the first two games of their 2026-2027 Concacaf Nations League campaign. Jamaica, drawn in Group B, will open the first round at the National Stadium against Guatemala on Friday, September 25, before welcoming Honduras four days later on Tuesday, September 29. Speid has selected a 24-man squad for the assignment. It will see the return to the Reggae Boyz squad for a number of players who last represented Jamaica in the failed World Cup 2026 qualifying campaign. Among them are goalkeeper and captain Andre Blake, wingers Leon Bailey and Tyreece Campbell, defender Richard King, midfielders Kasey Palmer and Karoy Anderson, and forward Renaldo Cephas. The top two teams from the two Nations League preliminary groups will qualify for the finals where they will be drawn alongside the ranked teams- two-time defending champions Mexico, the USA, Canada and Panama in the quarterfinals. See the full Reggae Boyz squad below. results.title: Should You Play Casual Or Classic Mode In Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave?
results.description: As a series, Fire Emblem has had two standout features compared to other tactical RPGs. First, characters can build relationships with their allies, and in more recent entries, even become romantically involved. Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave doesn't focus on the seduction side at all, preferring to show the camaraderie between teammates. The second feature, one that's been there since the first NES game, is that characters can permanently perish in combat. Fortune's Weave gives you this option at the beginning of the campaign as Classic Mode. Be warned: this is only for those seeking a brutal challenge. Casual Mode, on the other hand, is a more forgiving way to play through this gargantuan RPG, taking away the stress of potentially leading your allies to their demise. You also choose Normal or Hard difficulty modes, options that are separate from the Casual/Classic choice, so below we'll explain the differences between these key decisions. Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave difficult mode selection. Normal vs Hard Difficulty Mode The first choice is actually between Normal and Hard modes. The game describes Hard mode as "For experienced players", while Normal is for newcomers and "intermediate" players alike. If it's your first playthrough, we recommend going with Normal. If you wish for a challenge, Hard Mode adds extra constraints and ups the difficulty in several key factors. Here are the differences between them both: Normal Mode Hard Mode Enemies you face are around the recommended level. Enemies are at least three levels above the recommended cap. Fortuna's Blessing costs no Divine Sand. Fortuna's Blessing costs Divine Sand. Other Blessings cost a small amount of Divine Sand. Other Blessings cost more Divine Sand compared to Normal Mode. Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave classic or casual selections. Casual Mode vs Classic Mode If you've never played a Fire Emblem or similar tactical RPG before, go with Casual Mode. This eliminates all permadeath from the game, instead forcing fallen friendlies to retreat from the battle, returning only after its conclusion. Another more universally accepted term for Classic is 'Ironman Mode". If anyone in your party dies in combat, that's it. While you can always reverse time, either by restarting the chapter via the pause menu or sprinkling some of the Time Dust Fortuna bestows on your current Flame Lord early in their campaign, it's more useful here if any one of your roster kicks the bucket. However, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave adds a wrinkle to Classic Mode's definition of character death, and that's what happens when guest characters in any Heroic Games match fall in battle. If anyone who isn't designated as a group leader is defeated in combat, they will retreat. Since they're not currently part of your roster, you can still find them in Dagsion, give them gifts, invite them to share a meal, and eventually recruit them to your ranks. Progression can be carried over if you played the prologue prior to release. Can I Change These Settings Mid-Campaign? Yes, but it will take some time for them to kick in. On the title screen, provided you saved in the Obelisk as your named character (the default name is Eshmel), you can select the 'Descend Again' option. This lets you replay the prologue while giving you the opportunity to change the difficulty, swap between Casual and Classic modes, and tinker with your protagonist. The catch is that you need to replay the entire prologue. Thankfully, you can skip many things with the plus button, from cutscenes to battle screens and most dungeon fights. You will need to replay two full battles, but they're not that difficult to complete because your party is overpowered even in Hard Mode. Once you reach the Obelisk Chamber Base, you can continue each Flame Lord's story where you left it. You can also reduce the difficulty from Hard to Normal at the Shrine of Causality (the big glowing sun at the top of the stairs in the Base), but not increase from Normal to Hard.
